candidate_rule: two non-promoted evidence candidates per source record: verified fact and explicit scope limitation

documents.t: New Ofcom research reveals how to cut phone and internet bills
Signal struggles on trains widespread, Ofcom research finds

records.f: Average advertised broadband prices across different speed tiers fell by 6% in real terms over the previous year.
records.g: A market-average price movement does not prove the price, technology or availability offered at a specific address.

records.f: SIM-only plans accounted for half of pay-monthly mobile subscriptions, up from 44% one year earlier.
records.g: Subscription mix is a national market measure and does not establish mobile coverage or service quality at a parcel.

records.f: Average prices for SIM-only plans with unlimited data fell by 8% in real terms over the previous year.
records.g: Average tariff pricing cannot determine the plan available or suitable for an individual user or location.

records.f: Ofcom reported that SIM-only deals were available for less than £5 per month.
records.g: The existence of low-cost offers does not establish eligibility, contract terms, network coverage or lasting availability.

records.f: Ofcom's latest data indicated that 28% of broadband customers were out of contract.
records.g: Contract status is a consumer-market statistic and cannot identify the service state of a specific premises.

records.f: Broadband customers in contract spent on average between £7 and £9 per month less than out-of-contract customers.
records.g: The average saving is not a quote or guaranteed saving for an individual household.

records.f: Eighteen per cent of households switched internet provider in the latest year, up from 14% in 2023.
records.g: A national switching rate does not establish which providers can serve a particular address.

records.f: The One Touch Switch process introduced in September 2024 had been used by more than 2 million customers.
records.g: Use of a switching process does not prove successful activation or service availability at a specific parcel.

records.f: Ofcom stated that around eight in ten UK homes had access to full-fibre broadband.
records.g: This rounded national availability estimate must not be promoted to exact-address orderability without a current provider or UPRN check.

records.f: Mobile virtual network operators and major operators' budget brands had consistently offered deals between 40% and 50% cheaper than average prices.
records.g: Relative price positioning does not establish local network performance, eligibility or total contract cost.

records.f: Seventy per cent of households buying broadband and landline together made no outgoing landline call in the previous year.
records.g: Household usage behaviour cannot determine whether an individual premises requires or receives a landline service.

records.f: Standalone broadband typically cost about £7 per month less than broadband bundled with a landline.
records.g: A typical price difference is not an address-specific quotation and may exclude installation, promotional or contract conditions.

records.f: Twenty-nine per cent of pay-monthly mobile users consumed 2 GB of data or less per month.
records.g: National consumption distribution does not establish signal availability, congestion or user requirements at a location.

records.f: Thirty-nine per cent of pay-monthly customers took a service with more than 50 GB of inclusive data per month.
records.g: Tariff allowance selection does not prove actual local network capability or individual need.

records.f: Only 5% of pay-monthly customers used more than 50 GB of mobile data per month.
records.g: Aggregate usage does not measure coverage, achievable speed or reliability at an exact address.

records.f: Fifty-five per cent of pay-monthly mobile customers used 20% or less of their monthly data allowance.
records.g: Allowance utilisation is a consumer behaviour statistic and cannot determine parcel-level connectivity.

records.f: A further 17% of pay-monthly mobile customers used between 20% and 40% of their monthly data allowance.
records.g: The aggregate range does not establish service performance or suitable tariff size for a particular person.

records.f: Ofcom estimated that households bundling telecoms services generally saved between £26 and £48 per month compared with buying them separately.
records.g: Estimated bundle savings are not guaranteed and do not prove service availability or contract suitability at an address.

records.f: The estimated average contract price of pay TV in a bundle with broadband and landline fell by 23% in real terms to £12 per month.
records.g: The average bundled component price is not a retail quote and does not establish broadband availability at a premises.

records.f: Broadband social tariffs for people claiming certain benefits ranged from £12.50 to £24 per month.
records.g: The published range does not establish benefit eligibility, provider coverage or current product availability at a specific address.

records.f: The number of available social tariffs had grown from three in 2020 to more than 30.
records.g: A tariff count is market-level evidence and does not establish which tariff is accessible at a particular premises.

records.f: There were 532,000 customers using a social tariff in June 2025, 26,000 more than one year earlier.
records.g: National take-up does not identify eligible households or exact-address service options.

records.f: Ofcom reported that 70% of eligible households were unaware that social tariffs existed.
records.g: Survey-based awareness does not determine eligibility or availability for an individual household.

records.f: Mobile performance was poor on between 58% and 83% of tests carried out on trains, depending on the mobile network.
records.g: Results from measured railway segments do not predict performance on every train, route, carriage or journey.

records.f: The dedicated research measured mobile performance across 24 segments of key railway lines in England, Scotland and Wales.
records.g: The tested segments are a study sample and do not provide exhaustive national rail or address-level coverage.

records.f: The study defined good performance as at least 5 Mbit/s download, at least 1.5 Mbit/s upload and latency no greater than 50 milliseconds.
records.g: Meeting or missing this study threshold does not guarantee application performance for every passenger or device.

records.f: Good-performance standards were met on 42% of measured segments for EE, 21% for Three, 20% for O2 and 17% for Vodafone.
records.g: Operator percentages are aggregate study results and cannot determine performance at a specific point or time.

records.f: On-board Wi-Fi provided by train companies performed well in only 1% of the measurements.
records.g: The study result does not establish the current equipment or service on every train operator and route.

records.f: Ofcom stated that UK mobile networks had invested £10 billion since 2020 while the price of an average-use mobile basket fell by 20% in real terms between 2020 and 2025.
records.g: National investment and pricing trends do not prove local coverage, capacity or customer savings.

records.f: Ofcom reported that millimetre-wave spectrum had become available for mobile services in 68 high-density areas with high demand for mobile data.
records.g: Spectrum availability in designated areas does not prove deployment, indoor coverage, handset support or service at a particular premises.
